name: OpenTSDB
tagline: HBase-backed time-series database from the Hadoop era; still in service, rarely chosen for new work.
description: OpenTSDB stores metrics as rows in HBase (or Bigtable) behind stateless TSD daemons, which let early large-scale shops keep years of raw, undownsampled data on their Hadoop clusters. Its metric-plus-tags data model and simple telnet/HTTP put API influenced many later systems, and several modern TSDBs still accept the OpenTSDB protocol for compatibility. Development has largely stopped: the last stable release dates from 2021 and only a 2.5.0 release candidate followed in December 2024. Today it mostly matters for legacy installations and as an ingest format other databases import.
statusNote: Dormant: last stable release 2.4.1 (Sept 2021), 2.5.0-RC1 tagged Dec 2024 with no activity since. Prefer VictoriaMetrics, Mimir or TimescaleDB for new work.

scale.notes: Scales with the underlying HBase or Bigtable cluster; TSDs are stateless and added freely.

strengths: Keeps raw data indefinitely on HBase without downsampling
Stateless TSDs scale horizontally behind a load balancer
Fits shops that already run Hadoop/HBase
weaknesses: Requires operating HBase and ZooKeeper, which is heavy for a metrics store
No PromQL or SQL; query API is limited and slow on high-cardinality tags
No native retention or downsampling policies
useCases: Archival metrics on an existing HBase cluster
